subject: Electrical Engineering
title: 5G and OFDM: Signals for Speed
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on 5G and OFDM: Signals for Speed.

hook.text: 5G sends data on thousands of tiny sub-carriers simultaneously. Each one carries a piece.

buildup.text: OFDM splits a wideband channel into many narrow sub-channels, each modulated independently.

discovery.text: An inverse FFT at the transmitter and an FFT at the receiver handle all sub-carriers at once.

twist.text: OFDM is resilient to multipath — reflections off buildings affect only some sub-carriers, not all.

climax.text: Wi-Fi, LTE, 5G, and digital TV all use OFDM — the dominant modulation of the modern era.

punchline.text: Thousands of sub-carriers, one FFT — OFDM makes high-speed wireless reliable.

quiz.question: Why is OFDM resilient to multipath interference?
options: It uses very high transmission power to overpower reflections
Reflections affect only some sub-carriers, not the entire channel
It transmits data only when no reflections are present
